sources.entry: Build iOS Photo Library App with Xamarin and Visual Studio

summary.title: Building iOS Apps with Xamarin and Visual Studio
summary.one_liner: You learn how to set up a Windows and Mac toolchain (Visual Studio, Xamarin.iOS, Xcode) for building a basic iOS photo library viewer in C#.
takeaways: Xamarin lets you write iOS apps in C# with Visual Studio, with native API access via Xamarin.iOS.
Building for iOS with Xamarin on Windows needs a networked Mac with Xcode as a build host; a Mac VM is an alternative.
Xamarin Forms suits maximum code sharing, while Xamarin.iOS suits platform-specific or custom UI.
Setup involves installing Xcode and Xamarin on the Mac, then Visual Studio with the Xamarin workload on Windows.
summary.summary: This tutorial introduces building iOS apps with Xamarin and Visual Studio, explaining Xamarin's role as a cross-platform C# framework and how it compares to native development. It then walks through the environment setup: Xcode and Xamarin on a Mac build host, and Visual Studio with the Xamarin tools on Windows. The page is the setup and background section of a project where you build a simple iPhone app that displays a user's photo library. It assumes basic C# knowledge and no prior iOS experience.
